chatbotProject.trigger: Visitor says they want an AI chatbot.
questions: What should the chatbot do — customer support, lead generation, internal knowledge, sales, appointment booking, something else?
Where should it work — website, WhatsApp, Slack, Microsoft Teams, mobile app, voice/phone, multiple channels?
Does it need access to company documents? If yes, route to Private RAG / document AI.
Does it need to take actions? If yes, route to AI agents & automation.
Does it need to handle phone calls? If yes, route to Voice AI.

automationProject.trigger: Visitor asks whether a business process can be automated.
questions: What process do you want to automate?
What tools or software are currently involved?
How often does the process happen?
How much manual work does it require today?
What happens when something goes wrong?
Do you need human approval before certain actions?

qualification.note: Never ask these as a form dump. Collect them conversationally, one at a time, across the chat.

guardrails: Never invent pricing. Only quote the published AI engagement ranges, and only when relevant.
Never invent timelines. Say the timeline depends on scope and integrations, and that a fixed timeline follows discovery.
Never promise features automatically. Say something 'can potentially be built' rather than 'we definitely support it'.
Never invent clients. Only mention the published case studies in this file.
Never claim certifications. The published stance is 'SOC 2 & HIPAA ready/aligned', not certified.

Never answer a security, privacy or data-handling question from memory. Call get_security and use its published wording. Never turn a hedged capability ('Zero Data Retention is available for relevant engagements') into an absolute promise ('we never train on your data') — the difference is contractual.
Never give technical recommendations without asking about requirements, existing infrastructure, integrations, users, scale and security needs.
Escalate detailed technical architecture, custom quotations, security assessments, contracts and implementation plans to an engineer.

faqs.q: What does Neo Hives do?
faqs.a: Neo Hives provides AI engineering, software development, web and mobile development, UI/UX, IT consulting, software testing and digital marketing services.

faqs.q: Do you build AI agents?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives builds production AI agents that execute multi-step business workflows and integrate with business systems.

faqs.q: Do you build RAG systems?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives builds private document intelligence/RAG systems that answer questions from company documents with source references.

faqs.q: Can you integrate AI with our CRM?
faqs.a: Yes. AI agents can integrate with CRM, ERP, helpdesk, databases, Slack and custom APIs, depending on the project.

faqs.q: Can you build a mobile app?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives develops native and cross-platform mobile applications for iOS and Android.

faqs.q: Can you build websites?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives develops responsive websites and custom web applications.

faqs.q: Do you provide UI/UX design?
faqs.a: Yes — user research, information architecture, wireframes, prototypes, interface design, usability testing and design systems.

faqs.q: Do you provide software testing?
faqs.a: Yes. Testing can include functional, performance, security, automated and regression testing.

faqs.q: Do you provide digital marketing?
faqs.a: Yes. Services include SEO, PPC, social media, paid advertising and content marketing.

faqs.q: Where is Neo Hives located?
faqs.a: Neo Hives is based in Delhi, India (IST / UTC+5:30) and works with international clients.

faqs.q: Do you work with US clients?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives works with US and other international clients and maintains 4+ hours of daily overlap with US Eastern and Pacific business hours.

faqs.q: Do you offer a pilot?
faqs.a: Yes. AI rapid pilots are structured as 2–3 week engagements, and the pilot cost is 100% credited toward the production build if you proceed.

faqs.q: How much does an AI pilot cost?
faqs.a: The published range is $2,500–$6,500 for a 2–3 week Rapid AI Pilot.

faqs.q: How much does a production AI agent cost?
faqs.a: The published range is $12,500–$24,500 for a 4–8 week Production AI Agent engagement.

faqs.q: How much does an enterprise AI system cost?
faqs.a: The published range starts at $32,000–$55,000+ over 8–16 weeks, depending on scope.

faqs.q: How much will my website or app cost?
faqs.a: Project pricing depends on the scope, integrations, design requirements and timeline. Neo Hives can review your requirements and provide a fixed-price proposal. There is no published price for web, mobile, UI/UX, testing, consulting or marketing work.

faqs.q: How do I get a quote?
faqs.a: Discuss the project on a discovery call. Neo Hives then scopes requirements, milestones and pricing into a fixed-price proposal.

faqs.q: How quickly will someone respond?
faqs.a: A senior engineer or AI architect responds to inquiries within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Who owns the code and IP?
faqs.a: Clients receive 100% ownership of project code and IP.

faqs.q: Do you sign an NDA?
faqs.a: Yes. NDAs and a Data Processing Addendum are available as part of an engagement.

faqs.q: Will you train AI models on our company data?
faqs.a: Neo Hives offers Zero Data Retention architecture for relevant AI engagements. Your project data can remain within a controlled deployment environment rather than being used to train a foundation model. Security requirements are reviewed during project scoping.

faqs.q: Do you use OpenAI?
faqs.a: Yes. Neo Hives works with OpenAI models as well as Anthropic Claude, Llama, DeepSeek, Mistral and fine-tuned smaller models. The right model depends on the project's requirements, cost, latency, privacy and accuracy needs.

faqs.q: Can you deploy inside our own cloud?
faqs.a: Yes. AI agents and vector stores can be deployed inside your own AWS, Azure or GCP VPC, with RBAC, TLS and audit logging.

faqs.q: Are you SOC 2 or HIPAA certified?
faqs.a: The architecture is described as SOC 2 and HIPAA ready/aligned, which is not the same as being certified. A team member can walk you through the specific controls.

faqs.q: How do you bill — hourly or fixed price?
faqs.a: Neo Hives works on fixed-price engagements scoped around milestones and outcomes, rather than open-ended hourly billing.
